item.title: 'I would love to do my first Grand Tour' - US talent Artem Shmidt trades Netcompany Ineos for NSN Cycling
item.author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
item.content:encoded: His victory at the 1.Pro race in France on a rainy May edition saw him make an aggressive solo move to disrupt an expected battle of sprinters. His power, combined with tactical acumen, cast a sharp light on his growing versatility. “Artem Shmidt is one of the most exciting talents to come out of the US in recent years, and we believe he represents a rider profile we don’t currently have in the team,” said Kjell Carlstrom, NSN's general manager, in a press release Friday.“Artem already has some very clear qualities, particularly in the time trial, but what excites us is how much more he can develop over the next three seasons. He only has two seasons in the WorldTour to his name, and already he has shown great potential, so a big objective for us is to continue facilitating that development and see just how far he can go in one-day and stage races."Shmidt has developed from his junior years with LUX Cycling and Hot Tubes Development for two years on the Continental level with Hagens Berman Jayco. He was always comfortable and strong on a time trial bike, winning his first USPro title in the men's U23 ITT in 2024, then sweeping the elite title the next two years.A move to NSN is now an opportunity for Shmidt to develop for stage racing, his goal to earn a spot for a Grand Tour appearance, which would be his first.“In terms of my development in road racing, I believe NSN is the perfect team for me to develop an aggressive and opportunistic racing style and really sharpen those characteristics I have shown as a rider. My big objectives will naturally be the time trials and Spring Classics, but I would love to do my first Grand Tour," Shmidt said in the NSN announcement about his new contract."There were many things that stood out to me about NSN Cycling Team. The professionalism and the way the team came across in our meetings were important, but what really made an impact was the culture. The English-speaking environment and the atmosphere in the team were big factors for me, and the racing style is more my type of beat. "Being up the road, attacking, and on that front foot is the mentality that we share.”Shmidt will compete at Grands Prix Cyclistes Québec et Montréal for Netcompany Ineos and follow the Canadian doubleheader by representing Team USA at UCI Road World Championships in Montréal, riding in the elite men's time trial and road race.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Decathlon CMA CGM register for business in Switzerland – Could contractual benefits help them keep Paul Seixas?
item.author: Patrick Fletcher
item.content:encoded: The Decathlon CMA CGM team has registered for business in Switzerland, switching its paying agent from France in a move that’s understood to be linked to their fight to keep hold of their prized rider, Paul Seixas, in the long-term. The possibility of such a switch, which would save considerable sums of money in taxes, was first raised in the spring, but denied by the team management at the time. It has now come to fruition.A new entity has been listed at the Register of Commerce in Geneva, named 'DECATHLON CYCLING TEAM SUISSE SA'. Registered on August 17, it carries the names of the team’s two senior management figures, Dominique Serieys and Mathieu Charpentier, and concerns ‘the management and activity of a professional cycling team’. A spokesperson for the team has confirmed to that this will be the new company that operates the cycling team from 2027. In addition to the men’s WorldTour squad, this entity will also govern the team’s development squads and a new women’s team that’s launching in 2027.The team insist they are still a French outfit, and they will continue to be a French-registered team when it comes to their WorldTour license with the UCI. In addition, their headquarters will remain where they are in La Motte-Servolex, near the French Alps. What’s changing is the legal and administrative base of the company that runs the team, often referred to in cycling as the ‘paying agent’. All contracts, therefore, will be arranged according to Swiss law. The team have declined to comment on the reasons for this change. It is one that will come with a considerable financial benefit. It will, for starters, mean the team will not pay the higher level of social security contributions that are associated with French contracts. Marc Madiot, president of the French team Groupama-FDJ, has previously highlighted this uneven playing field, suggesting a rule whereby all teams must have their base in Switzerland, where the UCI operates. Where Seixas comes into this is that Decathlon CMA CGM will effectively be able to offer him a higher salary, as a lesser percentage of it would be going to the taxman. There has been intense speculation over Seixas’ future this spring as he has stormed to very top echelon of the sport with a string of astounding performances at just 19 years of age. As Tadej Pogačar dominates the sport, teams are queuing up for the next best thing and Decathlon have been facing a fight to keep him beyond his current contract, which expires at the end of 2027. Having already been aggressive in the transfer market this summer, this move will in theory allow them to be more competitive when it comes to offering him a new package. But it’s not just down to Seixas. The team has been growing in stature since the Decathlon came on board as a sponsor in 2022, and then took over full ownership of the team from AG2R La Mondiale at the start of this year.The injection of investment from the international sports retailing giant has already seen them referred to among the ‘super-team’ bracket of cycling’s WorldTour, and the move to Switzerland will only hone their financial muscle. item.title: Record Watch: Five Knicks benchmarks in jeopardy this season
item.author: John Gove
item.content:encoded: Defending a championship changes the vibe during regular-season play. When the goal is to repeat a championship in June, Tuesday night games in February can feel like a formality. Nobody wants to overexert a key player in a meaningless game on the off chance that he’ll blow a hammy. However, Mike Brown’s offense, built for another deep playoff run, can’t help but generate eye-popping stats all season long.Between the exploding scoreboards, higher possession counts, and New York’s elite playmakers and scorers, several Knicks records are suddenly at risk. Some of these benchmarks have survived nearly 40 years, while the ink for others is still wet in the books. A closer look at the roster and statistics suggests five specific franchise records could realistically fall this season. Let’s dive in.Single-Season 30-Point GamesCurrent Record: 36 games – Richie Guerin (1961-1962), Patrick Ewing (1989-90), Jalen Brunson (2023-24)2026-27 Season Target: 37 gamesThe current franchise mark for the most 30-point contest in a regular season is a three-way tie spanning three distinct eras of Knicks basketball. Richie Guerin established the benchmark during the fast-break pace of the early 1960s. Patrick Ewing matched it during his prime, dominating the post game-in and game-out while carrying the team on his broad shoulders and aching knees. Captain Jalen Brunson joined the two Hall of Famers two seasons ago during his rise to All-NBA status.Of every record on this list, this one is the most wobbly. Brunson remains the undisputed engine of New York’s half-court offense, combining incredible footwork with elite basketball smarts.In Mike Brown’s five-out system, defenses can no longer load up in the paint without leaving deadly perimeter shooters uncovered. Having Karl-Anthony Towns at center pulls defensive anchors 25 feet away from the basket, giving Brunson wider driving lanes, fewer double-teams, and access to his mid-range spots. Assuming he’ll be healthy all season (knock on wood and cross yourself), Brunson claiming sole possession of this record with 37-plus 30-point games feels more like a matter of when, not if.Single-Game Scoring RecordCurrent Record: 62 points – Carmelo Anthony (January 24, 2014 vs. Charlotte Bobcats)2026-27 Season Target: 63 pointsFirst, a moment of silence for the Charlotte Bobcats. . . . Okay, we’re good to go.Carmelo Anthony’s 62-point masterclass against Charlotte has stood untouched for 13 years. In a legendary isolation clinic, Melo shot 23-of-35 from the floor without recording a single assist or turnover. Surpassing a single-game point total like that requires the blend of crazy shot volume, incredible efficiency, (no small degree of selfishness,) and a game that’s competitive enough to keep starters on the floor late into the fourth quarter.New York’s current roster is different because it features distinct creators who can completely go off in a single game. Brunson already came within a single point of the record, dropping 61 points on 47 shot attempts against the Spurs in March 2024. Meanwhile, Towns brings a personal career-high of 62 points from his time in Minnesota, with an outside stroke that can cause box score chaos. If Towns hits six or seven early threes while dominating the glass, or if Brunson takes over a high-paced track meet, Carmelo’s iconic record could melt like a stick of butter on a sunny afternoon.Single Season Team 3-PointersCurrent Record: 1,168 made three-pointers (2025-26)2026-27 Season Target: 1,169 made three-pointersNew York set a new record last season, draining 1,168 three-pointers. And Mike Brown’s Knicks are just getting started.Brown’s scheme relies heavily on five-out principles that are designed to distort perimeter coverage. With movement shooters on the bench (Shamet, McBride, and occasionally Alvarado and Clarkson), the sheer volume of perimeter attempts is bound to increase. Averaging roughly 14 made threes a game across a full schedule, and thereby breaking their own team record for a second straight season, seems like the natural trajectory for this squad.Individual Single Season 3-PointersCurrent Record: 283 made three-pointers – Donte DiVincenzo (2023-24 season)2026-27 Season Target: 284 made three-pointersWhen Donte DiVincenzo poured in 283 three-pointers during his lone full season with the Knicks, he shattered Evan Fournier’s previous mark of 241, setting an incredible bar for perimeter volume. Reaching that total requires a player to average roughly 3.5 made threes per game while appearing in almost every matchup.DiVincenzo and Fournier are long gone, but the team has redistributed the heavy perimeter workload across its primary offensive tools. Both Towns and Brunson shoot near 40% from beyond the arc and often get the green light in Brown’s system. If KAT maintains a high-volume, trailing-center role in transition, or if Cap takes even more off-dribble pull-up jumpers, DiVo’s record could easily be squashed before the season’s end.Single Season Point TotalCurrent Record: 2,347 points – Patrick Ewing (1989-90 season)2026-27 Season Target: 2,348 pointsEwing’s 1989-90 campaign remains the ultimate test of single-season scoring in franchise history. Piling up 2,347 total points, Ewing averaged 28.6 points per contest and played all 82 games. Obviously, the big fella served as the team’s primary generator and carried most of the load that year.Surpassing Ewing’s record is hands-down the most grueling challenge on this list of beatable benchmarks. Per-game averages mean little if a player misses games due to load management or minor injury, so any absence from the floor will interrupt the scoring pace needed to top Patrick. Across 77 appearances in 2023-24, Brunson recorded 2,212 points, which put him within spitting distance of the record. To beat out Ewing, Jalen would need to maintain a scoring average north of 28 points per game, while playing in at least 80 contests. Requiring a combination of elite offensive production and availability, the 2,348 points in a season is the hardest to crack, and as Jalen enters his thirties, Coach Brown is likely to play Jalen for shorter stints in unimportant games, to preserve him for the offseason. Still, it is mathematically within reach.Some franchise records are so incredible that they’re unlikely to be toppled, given the changes in play-style, rules, and rosters over time. However, Mike Brown’s team, based on a high-volume, high-efficiency attack, is not your father’s Knicks. In the 1995-96 season, the ‘Bockers averaged 97.2 points per game and attempted 1,285 three-pointers; thirty years later, they averaged 116.5 PPG and took 3,133 threes. And that’s not even top-five in the league! (The Warriors tried 3,616.) With the firepower currently employed at MSG, some of these historical benchmarks are truly at risk.Which records do you think will fall this year? Talk about it below!

item.title: Champions League review: Irish heroics, rejected resignations and Mourinho’s return
item.author: John Brewin
item.content:encoded: The league phase has begun. From Olise’s brilliance to Sabah’s pub cleaner turned quiz contestant turned manager, there was plenty to talk aboutThe league phase has been previewed as first step toward reclaiming a crown last lifted in 2015, with disappointments aplenty since. Lionel Messi claiming just one Champions League title in the last decade of his time at Camp Nou is the starkest statistic. The player anointed as Messi’s successor, Lamine Yamal, is already a European and world champion for Spain, so this is the next frontier. A soggy Wednesday evening at Camp Nou saw Hansi Flick’s team show their attacking chops remain of the highest quality in a 5-1 defeat of Feyenoord. The club presidential regime of Joan Laporta continues to pull levers to confound financial experts, with Gabriel Jesus, one of the summer’s arrivals, scoring his first Barca goal. Yamal got on the scoresheet via a scruffy free-kick after Raphinha had reminded there are further dimensions to that all-star attack, his first goal of his pair two sending Feyenoord defenders skidding.Continue reading...

item.title: 'The last year I don't think we've done a single aero test' –Why time trials are no longer a major focus for Primož Roglič and why the Vuelta TT did not go as Red Bull predicted
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: Just 1km shorter than Thursday's TT at La Vuelta, Roglič gained 1:38 over the Spaniard on that day. If they wanted to completely overhaul Mas and take the red jersey, they were going to need more – 2:10 to be precise – after Mas had eked out his advantage with superiority in the mountains.When the dust settled on Roglič's and Mas' efforts into Jerez, there was to be no miracle switch, with the red jersey defending his lead superbly to finish just 33 seconds slower than the rival who has long been beating him at the Vuelta. What had gone wrong for Roglič? In reality, not much. When his sports directors came to speak to the press, Sven Vanthourenhout stressed how he had done 'everything perfect', which team Head of Engineering Dan Bigham confirmed was the numerical truth, not just the right answer at the time from the team. It was more a case of Mas riding the TT of his career, much as he claimed this was not the case, but it's fair to say Red Bull were not expecting the gap between the two to be so relatively narrow."Roglič had a good last sector, but then, to be honest, so did Mas, and he really outperformed our models, which is reflective of where Mas is in the race, and you can't really ignore it," Bigham told outside the packed Red Bull team bus on Thursday. "He has been by some margin the best climber, and today did his best time trial probably ever, I would say actually, [but] I need to check the numbers and see how it pans out."But [Felix] Gall was within about 10 seconds or so versus our prediction. Callum [Thornley] was actually a second slower. Roglič was seven seconds quicker. Finn [Fisher-Black] was nine seconds quicker. So we're within 10 seconds on most of our predictions for the guys who have numbers on, and yeah, Mas was just a whole lot faster than probably you would have stuck a number on three weeks ago."Given the context of not being able to train on his TT bike before the Vuelta at all, due to being hit by a driver in training near Livigno, Roglič himself was delighted with the performance, simply conceding that Mas was untouchable for the moment. Two mountain stages remain, but what we've seen ever since Mas inherited red is that there's a considerable gap between the two when it comes to climbing. The time trial was Roglič's big chance. Time trials no longer a major focus for RogličRoglič remains in the upper echelon, but was once one of the absolute best time trial riders in the world, winning eight Grand Tour ITT stages down the years, an Olympic title in Tokyo, and finishing second at the World Championships in 2017.There was talk at the start of Roglič not riding the same developmental model of Specialized TT bike that Remco Evenepoel had access to at the Tour. But Bigham also revealed the lack of time the Slovenian has been dedicating to time trialling in what will be his final year on Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe. "So in my first year, I worked with him quite a bit, and we did quite a lot of testing," Bigham told . "To be honest, the last year, I don't think we've done a single aero test, which is probably more of a reflection on where he feels he is in his position and what evolution he wants or doesn't want, and also what he wants to focus on. "Obviously, family is one big important thing for him, but also at the same time, his ambitions require him to just train a lot. And his opinion was he didn't think he could evolve his position any further, so he wasn't that fussed by doing more testing."While it's an important point to note, and perhaps could have meant for a few seconds gained here and there on the course on Thursday, Bigham was certain that it wouldn't have done much in the way of pulling back the extra time he required to really move closer to Mas' hold on red."No, not particularly," he said when asked whether the change in focus was a major factor. "No, I don't think if I'd spent more time with him, we would have found – what did we need, 90 seconds? So yeah, I mean 90 seconds on this course-that's about 45 watts. I'm not finding 45 watts. That's about 12% drag reduction. I can dream of that, but yeah."Focusing on the younger ridersBigham also pointed to how Red Bull's focus as one of the top teams when it comes to ITT research and development is mostly aimed at their up-and-coming generation of riders. With the best rider against the clock in the world among their ranks in Evenepoel, the potential trickle-down effect of his influence, Bigham's, and all of the Engineering team at the German WorldTour squad was visible in the top performances of Callum Thornley, who finished second on stage 18, and Finn Fisher-Black in sixth. "There's only so many tests that you can run over a year, and if you're going to pick anybody, you invest in that next generation that are coming through," explained Bigham. "Callum's obviously a great example of this, and Finn's had a lot of work as well. But also people like [Giulio] Pellizzari, like Luke Tuckwell, these are the guys who are going to be winning us races for the next five to 10 years. We want to invest early because this kind of stuff compounds. "It's not just that you find improvement and it's lost. You find improvement, and you keep building on that. You adapt, you get better, and you keep improving. And you've got to start that process early, when they're in the Devo team, which is a great thing for us. "We have under-19, under-23, and obviously World Tour teams. We have a great conveyor belt there. We have so many riders who are coming through and continue to come through. But it just means that my job ends up being working with the younger guys to make sure we put them in a good position. So when they get to the World Tour, it's fine-tuning and not drastic changes."In the end, drastic changes would not have changed much for Primož Roglič in his pursuit of red in the TT, but he was at peace with that, and with Red Bull admitting that Mas simply performed much better than any of their models could predict, they will simply have to live with that. Only an unpredictable miracle in the mountains from the four-time Vuelta winner can turn this race around now.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!

item.title: Knicks’ interest in veteran free-agent center emerges ahead of training camp
item.author: Antonio Losada
item.content:encoded: The New York Knicks have Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond positioned atop their center depth chart, but the defending champions remain without a traditional third center as training camp approaches and this saga doesn’t feel any closer to an end.In yet another update on the situation, according to SNY’s Ian Begley, veteran free agent Tony Bradley has emerged on the Knicks’ radar as New York continues evaluating potential additions for its remaining roster spots, with a competition for those expected to take place throughout camp and the preseason.“One other note on free agent signings ahead of training camp: veteran center Tony Bradley has also been a player on the Knicks’ radar,” Begley reported.If you’re like me, you probably though Bradley was 35 already. Turns out he’s only 28!Even then, and while Bradley would provide an experienced third option behind Towns and Drummond, don’t expect TB (or whoever ends up landing in New York) to find a clear and open path into coach Mike Brown’s established rotation.Begley noted that the Knicks are comfortable with their current top two options despite the absence of another traditional center, making it even tougher for Mystery Man to get any potential playing time.“The Knicks do not currently have a third center, but there is a strong degree of confidence internally in the Karl-Anthony Towns-Andre Drummond duo at the position,” Begley reported.Bradley spent last season with the Indiana Pacers and Atlanta Hawks, appearing in 41 games and averaging 4.0 points and 2.8 rebounds in 11 minutes per game.The 6-foot-10 center has eight seasons of NBA experience after entering the league as the No. 28 overall pick in the 2017 NBA Draft. Bradley owns career averages of 4.3 points and 3.8 rebounds in 234 regular-season appearances.Begley previously reported that New York has also shown interest in free agents Drew Eubanks and John Konchar while evaluating its remaining roster openings, hinting at the openness of the Knicks’ brass to land a variety of player types ahead of their title defense.For now, the Knicks’ next step is opening training camp before they face the Philadelphia 76ers in the first game of the preseason.

item.title: Season over for Pauline Ferrand-Prévot
item.author: Patrick Fletcher
item.content:encoded: She has not raced since and, after reports that she would skip the World Championships, it's now clear that she will not race again this year. "In consultation with the team, it has been decided that Pauline will take the time to rest and recover for the remainder of the season," read a statement from the Visma-Lease a Bike team,"We wish Pauline all the best for the weeks ahead and look forward to seeing her racing with the team next season."After dominating the Tour last year, Ferrand-Prévot fell completely flat this time around, losing time in the time trial and in the punchy stages before the race even reached the critical summit finish at Mont Ventoux. By that point, she was down in 14th place, 14 minutes behind the leader, and the Bald Mountain would turn out to be the scene of her final pedal strokes in the race and in her season. Ferrand-Prévot had initially brushed aside any underlying issues, suggesting the level of the peloton had simply increased and even revealing she hit personal power records as she was getting dropped on stage 5. However, in announcing her exit from the race ahead of stage 8, the team stated that she "was not feeling well this morning", and Ferrand-Prévot stated: "I had to quit the race after being sick on the Friday night."It would now appear there's a bigger issue at play, with the team highlighting the need to "rest and recover" for the final months of the season. Ferrand-Prévot therefore ends her 2026 campaign, without a win, despite going close at the Tour of Flanders, where she was the runner-up, and Paris-Roubaix, where she was third as she and teammate Marianne Vos were outfoxed by Franziska Koch.She rode a fairly quiet Vuelta Femenina before turning to the Tour de France, where she was expected to lead the charge for yellow once again but where her season ultimately ended prematurely.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: As it happened: Stalemate among the GC favourites as win goes to the breakaway on stage 19 of the Vuelta a España
item.author: Stephen Puddicombe
item.content:encoded: For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go! Hello and welcome to stage 19 of the Vuelta a España! September 11, 2026 – 5:54 AMThere was a sense after yesterday’s time trial that Enric Mas had passed the all-important test at yesterday’s time trial, holding off the challenge by Primož Roglič in a discipline he excels less at with a healthy lead at the top of the classification still intactHowever, this race is far from over - and today’s parcours is prime territory for an ambush. As one of the few to exceed 200km , and with plenty of climbing along the way, including a summit finish, both he and his Movistar team must be alert, and again need to rise to the occasion. September 11, 2026 – 6:02 AMThe riders are in the neutralised zone, but one rider not among them is yesterday’s winner Stefan Küng. That victory made it mission accomplished at this Vuelta for the Swiss time trialist specialist, as well as delivering his Tudor team a second victory following Marco Brenner’s success - a fantastic return for one of the race’s smaller teams. September 11, 2026 – 6:11 AMAnd they're off! The first third of this flat stage is flat, so it could take a while for a break to form. The riders best brace themselves for a long battle.September 11, 2026 – 6:20 AMThe attacks are, as expected, coming thick and fast! For the time being we have a group of eight up the road by a few seconds but the situation is very much in flux.Here were the riders at the start, before hostilities began. September 11, 2026 – 6:30 AMHannes Wilksch and Mats Wenzel were the latest to try a move, but, along with a flurry of poursuivants, have all be swept up back into the peloton. The latter's Equipo Kern Pharma is especially eager for some success today, given the doubt surrounding their future as they continue to seek a new sponsor.September 11, 2026 – 6:37 AMThere have been plenty of attacks, but still nothing sticking, an 8-man group the latest to try to no avail. This looks set to go on for a while longer yet.September 11, 2026 – 6:44 AMPaul Double has abandoned the race. There's been no crash we're aware of, but the Brit has been struggling at this Vuelta, and was second-to-last at the bottom of the GC. Hard-going for a man whois primarily a climber. September 11, 2026 – 6:51 AM Jasha Sütterlin, stage winner Andreas Leknessund and soon-to-retire Steven Kruijswijk are the latest to try an attack. It's great to see the latter on the move and having some fun for himself, having done so much tireless work at the front of this Vuelta controlling the race for his Visma teammates Wout van Aert and Matthew Brennan. What a story it would be if he could take a stage win on the last Grand Tour of his career. September 11, 2026 – 6:57 AMAfter 40km of attacking, this trio of Leknessund, Kruijswijk and Sütterlin is the first to manage to stay out for some time and build a promising lead. They've got 25 seconds as things stand. September 11, 2026 – 7:04 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 11, 2026 – 7:10 AMLeknessund, Kruijswijk and Sütterlin are still leading, now 45 seconds up on the peloton. In between, some chasers are trying to join them. The fight is still on an the intensity remains high.September 11, 2026 – 7:17 AMThere is plenty of firepower in the chase group trying to join Leknessund, Kruijswijk and Sütterlin. Oliveira, Johannessen, Tronchon and Weiss have formed a quartet, and are now just 10 seconds behind, and 30 seconds ahead of the peloton, where things still haven't settled down. September 11, 2026 – 7:24 AMOliveira, Tronchon, and Johannessen (but not Weiess - he's dropped back) have now bridged up to Leknessund, Kruijswijk and Sütterlin, but the new front group are only a mere 20 seconds ahead of the peloton. It seems like there is enough in the peloton unhappy with the situation to not allow them to form the day's break. September 11, 2026 – 7:29 AMThe irrepressible Kevin Vermaerke is on the attack again. Aware that he's a superior climber, his UAE teammate Oliveira dropped back to pace him, and the duo have just joined the five leaders. Together, they're now 35 seconds ahead of the peloton. September 11, 2026 – 7:34 AMThis leading group of seven is working well together, and have built a lead of 47 - which must be the biggest gap any group has managed all day so far. The action is still very on in the peloton, where the attacks keep coming, and promises to continue to do so when they reach the day's first climb in just a few kilometres. September 11, 2026 – 7:41 AMThe riders are on the Puerto de las Abejas, the first of the day's three climbs. It's not the hardest of the day, averaging just 4.3%, but its length of 14.6km will ensure that climbers who want to get into the break have a chance.One such rider is Santiago Buitrago, who Pello Bilbao attempted to launch up the road, but he has managed to go clear of the peloton yet. As it stands, there are 30 seconds between them in the peloton and the seven leaders up the road. September 11, 2026 – 7:51 AMThe constant action at the front of the peloton as more riders try to escape to join the break on the climb is keeping the lead group (picture below, although it's now made up of seven riders, since Sütterlin was dropped) well within sight. They're just a few seconds ahead, and the battle to form the break is far from over. September 11, 2026 – 7:57 AMVimsa-Lease a Bike are hatching a plan for Sepp Kuss. Kruijswijk dropped back from the front group to help pace him up after attacking from the peloton. So far, though, he hasn't been able to join up to the leaders; nor has anyone else in the peloton, which remains 10 seconds behind the leaders as they climb the final 5km to the summit. September 11, 2026 – 8:06 AMA few riders have managed to join the leaders - Zana, Van Bekkum and Faura. Plus Eddie Dunbar, who bridged up earlier. While the break and the peloton remain so close on the road, the race is very much in flux.September 11, 2026 – 8:11 AMLeknessund led the lead group over the top of the climb, and since then they have been joined by a group of chasers. Briefly it looked as though Oscar Onley might be join, too, as he tried a cheeky attack, but the Brit (who is 5th on GC) did not manage to slip clear. As they descend, the leaders are 20 seconds ahead of the peloton).September 11, 2026 – 8:18 AMThis has been a truly relentless start to the stage, but there are signs, at last, that things might be about to calm down. For the first time all day, the peloton bunched up at the front, an indication that many are wanting to let the break go clear.But there are still some unhappy and wanting to join the leaders up the road, and another flurry of attacks begins. September 11, 2026 – 8:24 AMWe're almost halfway into the stage, and the race has just all come back together! Numerous riders had joined the lead group, to swell it to about 20 riders, but Netcompany Ineos paced at the front of the peloton to bring it back. The peloton is much smaller now as a result of how high the pace has been, but as things stand, there is no breakaway group. September 11, 2026 – 8:30 AMSo the action has re-set, and a new wave of attacks have come as riders try to form a new break. This has gone on for over 100km now - surely the longest battle to form a break at this Vuelta, and possible of the whole season. September 11, 2026 – 8:34 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 11, 2026 – 8:38 AMThe riders have been climbing the category two Puerto del Viento (the penultimate climb of the day; officially, at least), and Eddie Dunbar had managed to build a bit of a lead. He's being chased down by another group of hopefuls, among whom include the King of the Mountains Santiago Buitrago. September 11, 2026 – 8:43 AMDunbar continues to lead the race over the top of the climb, and so takes the KOM points. Behind follows a chase group of about 20 riders, about 15 seconds behind, including Buitrago.It's looking more promising for that group to join up to Dunbar and (finally) form the break of the day, as the peloton is about a minute adrift. But things still haven't settled, and more attacks come out of it as they near the summit. September 11, 2026 – 8:48 AMRichard Carapaz is at it again! The man in fourth-place on GC has used the descent of the climb to try and catch his rivals napping, and is part of small group that has a gap of a few seconds over the peloton. He's 5:17 down on Mas, but not the kind of man he can afford to give too much leeway to. September 11, 2026 – 8:53 AMYou sense EF have been hatching a plan all day, having been active at the front, and as one of the teams especially keen not to let the early breaks go clear. They've now succeeded in getting Carapaz up the road, but will be frustrated that their GC rivals are on the defensive - at the front of the peloton, Movistar are receiving help from Decathlon and Netcompany. September 11, 2026 – 8:57 AMDecathlon are doing the bulk of the chasing at the front of the peloton, rather than Mas’ Movistar, and have sent Sander De Pestel from the lead group to help the pace-setting.This is in defence of their leader Gall’s third place on GC, and it’s an undeniably defensive tactic - if they were being bolder, and intended to try to put Mas under pressure, they could have forced him to use up his Movistar teammates to bring Carapaz back, and then try to put the isolated red jersey under pressure with attacks.September 11, 2026 – 9:03 AMCarapaz's venture is over, as the peloton bring him back. His group managed to get a lead of about 30 seconds, but his GC rivals were not happy to let him build upon that.That means there's only one group now ahead of the peloton - a lead group of about 15 riders, about 1:30 ahead, and featuring Buitrago, and G Martin (who, in 13th, i the highest placed man on GC in it).September 11, 2026 – 9:11 AMThings have, at long last, settled down. Ever since bringing back the Carapaz chase group, the peloton has slowed down, allowing the lead group of 16 riders to build a lead of 2:30. We at last have a clear break of the day.The problem is, they don't have very long to build enough of a lead to hold off the chase from the peloton later on, with just 60km left to ride until arriving at the foot of the final climb. The break will have to work well to give themselves a chance of making it to the finish to contest for the stage win. September 11, 2026 – 9:19 AMIf this breakaway is to succeed, it will be the first stage since last Thursday will be won from a rider not representing either Visma-Lease a Bike or Tudor Pro Cycling, who have enjoyed a sweep of wins lately with their respective men Wout van Aert and Matthew Brennan, and Marco Brenner and Stefan Küng. Both teams failed to get anyone in the break today.September 11, 2026 – 9:26 AMBoth Pinarello and Groupama-FDJ (save for Tronchon’s stage win) have been quiet for most of this Vuelta, but are doing a great job today, having each got three riders into the breakaway. Also with multiple riders in it are Equipo Kern Pharma and Bahrain-Victorious with two each. September 11, 2026 – 9:32 AMMovistar have implemented the same plan that has served them so well since Enric Mas took the red jersey, putting Pablo Castrillo up the road as a satellite rider for later on. The remainder of their roster are setting the pace at the front of the peloton, with assistance from Onley’s Netompany Ineos team.Mas and Movistar again look firmly in control, after a very successful time trial yesterday. Mas is clearly feeling very confident, and not holding back talking about what great shape he’s in.September 11, 2026 – 9:39 AMNot fussed about the stage win, and instead focussed on defending the red jersey, Movistar are happy to set a light tempo and allow the break a big lead approaching five minutes. September 11, 2026 – 9:44 AMWhat will Felix Gall do today? He lost his 2nd place on GC to Primož Roglič on yesterday’s time trial, and was put on the defensive again earlier in the stage when the man directly behind him on GC, Richard Carapaz, went on the attack.We’re approaching his territory again, with a big summit finish at the end of this stage. With 1:24 to make up to take second place back from Roglič again ,we can expect him to make an attack.September 11, 2026 – 9:50 AMYesterday felt like Primož Roglič’s big chance to make a move on to challenge Enric Mas, but though he didn’t make the kind of inroads many expected of him, that does not mean his bid for the red jersey is over.Roglič has revealed that time trialling has not been a focus of his lately; which would imply that we shouldn’t read too much into his climbing form based on his time trialling form. He’s still got the ability, know-how and desire to put Mas under pressure on today’s final climb. September 11, 2026 – 9:56 AMThe riders have reached the bottom of the downhill they've been descending, and now must ride about 20km of valley road before arriving at the foot of the final climb of Peñas Blancas. The break's lead has been held at 4:45, which is a healthy one, but not enough to guarantee that the stage winner will come from one of them.September 11, 2026 – 10:01 AMFor unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. You'll get comprehensive race coverage of La Vuelta a España, subscriber-exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!September 11, 2026 – 10:08 AMThe break have done a great job on this valley section, and increased their lead to over 6 and a half minutes. It does now look as though they will survive to fight for the stage win. September 11, 2026 – 10:15 AMSo who from the break looks the most likely to win the stage?Guillaume Martin is the best-placed on GC, but could find himself prioritising making as many gains as possible rather than engaging in the tactical battle to win the stage - a situation he regularly finds himself in, having not taken a stage win yet in any of his many Grand Tour appearances.September 11, 2026 – 10:18 AMLeknessund certainly has the know-how, having taken a stage already earlier in the Vuelta; as does Eddie Dunbar, who claimed a couple at the Vuelta two years ago. The difficulty of the climb could suit him more than it does Leknessund.And as King of the Mountains, Buitrago is a prominent presence who ought to do well on such a finish, and is seeking a first Vuelta stage win having previously won twice at the Giro.September 11, 2026 – 10:24 AMThe riders are onto the final climb of the day! It officially climbs at 6.5% for 18.8km, but that average gradient takes into account some much gentler segments - there actual climb is far harder than those stats make it sound. It's long and enough and has sections that are steep enough to cause big time losses for anyone dropped early. This is set to be a thrilling fight for the stage win, and a dramatic one in the race for GC.September 11, 2026 – 10:28 AMThere's an early attack on the climb in the breakaway group, as Molard tries to get up the road; possibly as a satellite rider for Martin. He's dangling a few seconds ahead of the rest.In the peloton, it's Red Bull-Bora Hansgrohe who are leading on the lower slopes. They must have something planned for Primož Roglič.September 11, 2026 – 10:34 AMMolard has been brought back after his attack, and the break remains all together. That won't last, once the gradient kicks up and the climb starts to get serious. Meanwhile in the peloton, it's still Red Bull leading, showing impressive strength in numbers. September 11, 2026 – 10:37 AMAfter a long turn from his teammate Miguel, Buitrago has attacked from the breakaway group. So far only two riders have gone with him - Gloag, and, a few bike-lengths behind, Dunbar. September 11, 2026 – 10:42 AMRed Bull are trying to put him under pressure, but for now Mas remains comfortable in the peloton.Up ahead in the break, Berrade has joined the leading trio, while Castrillo is also trying to bridge up to them - he's clearly been given some freedom to ride for himself today. Movistar must be feeling confidant. September 11, 2026 – 10:46 AMRed Bull still lead the peloton with numerous riders, but the pace isn't especially high as reflected by the large number of riders still in the peloton.The break is also managing to hold a big lead over them, with an advantage now over seven minutes. If it wasn't already beyond doubt that they would contest the stage, it now surely is. September 11, 2026 – 10:51 AMA change in the peloton, as Movistar take over from Red Bull. They still have two teammates (Garcia Pierna and Romeo) to work for Mas, with Castrillo also up the road in reserve.Castrillo is also now losing ground to the leaders, and has been caught and passed by both Leknessund and Camprubí. His hopes of winning a stage are disappearing, so he may be called back by his team. September 11, 2026 – 10:57 AMStill no attacks from the peloton, but there is no a change at the front as EF take over. That suggests Carapaz is going to try something, having failed with an attack earlier.September 11, 2026 – 11:00 AMThere are still about 20 riders in the peloton, but not among them is Skjelmose, who has just been dropped. He's set to fall further down the GC, having dropped to eighth yesterday. September 11, 2026 – 11:05 AMAt the front, it's still the same four riders together - Buitrago, Gloag, Berrade and Dunbar. None of them have attacked each other yet, but will have to soon as the summit nears. September 11, 2026 – 11:06 AMMoments after that post, Buitrago attacked - and it's a deadly one! He's got a gap of ten seconds already, and looks very strong. Could this be the stage-winning move?September 11, 2026 – 11:09 AMDunbar is trying to chase Buitrago by himself, but still has ten seconds to make up as he goes under the flamme rouge.In the peloton, EF's Rodriguez has finished his long turn, but no attack has come yet from his teammate Carapaz.September 11, 2026 – 11:10 AMDunbar has closed in on Buitrago and caught him with less than 500m to ride...and now he goes straight past him! It looks like Dunbar is riding to victory. September 11, 2026 – 11:11 AMThe Irishman has done it, soloing the final few hundred metres to take the stage win. Buitrago comes home about 15 seconds later, with the consolation prize of a second-place finish and some more points in his KOM defence. September 11, 2026 – 11:12 AMAnd now Roglič makes his move! It's not an especially explosive one, though, and Mas, Onley, Gall and Carapaz can all follow him. September 11, 2026 – 11:14 AMOmrzel managed to claw his way back to the group, and the pace is slow enough for him to attack out of it. There's a stalemate in the group of favourites as they enter the final kilometre. September 11, 2026 – 11:16 AMMas takes control for the final metres of the climb to bring Omrzel back, and then Carapaz leads them over the finish line in the final sprint. Nothing separates the top GC favourites at the line, so it's as you were going into tomorrow's final mountain stage. September 11, 2026 – 11:18 AMThe winner today, Eddie Dunbar!September 11, 2026 – 11:28 AMHe was in defensive mode rather than aggressive today, but that was another day successfully navigated for Enric Mas. He didn't look under any pressure all day, and despite a lot of threats to attack in the GC group on the final climb, a move only came inside the final 2km from Primož Roglič, which he was able to answer. September 11, 2026 – 11:31 AMEdward Dunbar (Irl) Pinarello-Q36.5Santiago Buitrago (Col) Bahrain VictoriousThomas Gloag (GBr) Pinarello-Q36.5Urko Berrade Fernandez (Spa) Kern PharmaMarcel Camprubi Pijuan (Spa) Pinarello-Q36.5Andreas Leknessund (Nor) Uno-X MobilityGuillaume Martin Guyonnet (Fra) Groupama-FDJ UnitedChristopher Hamilton (Aus) Picnic PostNLKevin Vermaerke (USA) UAE Team Emirates XRGSergio Samitier (Spa) CofidisSeptember 11, 2026 – 11:34 AMPrimoz Roglic (Slo) Red Bull-Bora-HansgroheFélix Gall (Aut) Decathlon CMA CGMRichard Carapaz (Ecu) EF Education-EasyPostOscar Onley (GBr) Netcompany IneosJakob Omrzel (Slo) Bahrain VictoriousClément Berthet (Fra) Groupama-FDJ UnitedCristian Rodriguez (Spa) XDS AstanaMattias Skjelmose (Den) Lidl-TrekHarold Tejada (Col) XDS AstanaSeptember 11, 2026 – 11:41 AMAt the end of a long, epic stage of the Vuelta, which witnessed the longest battle to get into the break we've seen so far at the race, it was Eddie Dunbar who ultimately came out on top.The GC race didn't see much movement, with the top five coming home together, and just the one change in the GC as Skjelmose and Rodríguez swapped places. Have a read of our full report here.September 11, 2026 – 11:54 AMThanks for joining us today! Enric Mas managed to make it through today unscathed, but tomorrow could be another matter. item.title: The morning after winning the time trial, Stefan Küng pulls out of the Vuelta a España
item.author: Owen Rogers
item.content:encoded: Winner of the Vuelta a España’s stage 18 time trial, Stefan Küng has abandoned the race, reputedly to concentrate on the upcoming World Championships in Montréal.The Tudor Pro Cycling rider put in a blistering ride to win Thursday’s 32.1km individual time trial by almost three seconds, ahead of Briton Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), and is clearly keen to capitalise on the fine form which also brought him victory in the Tour de Pologne closing stage TT.With just 11 days until the Worlds TT, Küng will head to Canada to ensure he is in the best possible shape to take his first elite rainbow jersey. An accomplished Classics rider, Küng is primarly a specialist against the clock, and while he has multiple Swiss national titles to his name and is a double European champion, he has never won the individual time trial at Worlds, though he has been incredibly consistent.His best result came in 2022 in Wollongong, Australia, where he finished second, he was third in 2020 and has bagged a number of other top 10 finishes over the years."After completing 18 tough stages and winning yesterday's time trial at the Vuelta, both Stefan and the team have agreed that it is best for him to withdraw now," his Tudo Pro Cycling team said in a statement, according to Het Nieuwsblad. "Given the short turnaround between the end of the Vuelta and the time trial at the World Championships, and the exertion involved in international travel, this decision allows him to recover and fully prepare for the World Championships in Montréal, where he will compete in the individual time trial, the mixed relay, and the road race." While the World Championships time trial is 7km longer than Küng's victorious stage 18 Vuelta test, at 39.2km it is similar, especially with a relatively flat profile containing 200m of elevation. And on the form Küng has shown this summer, he will certainly start the race on September 20 as one of the favourites.This has not been an easy year for the 32-year-old Swiss rider. Joining the Tudor team at the start of the season, he crashed at Omloop Nieuwsblad, breaking his femur and spending a long period off the bike. He returned for the Swiss national championships in June, then took the stage win in Poland in August, though he only managed to take 12th place behind Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) in the Vuelta’s opening-day TT in Monaco.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Russell set to take F1 engine penalty after Mercedes introduces power unit upgrade
Is Isaac del Toro the new favourite for the World Championships? He says no but the road may say differently
item.author: Matilda Price
item.content:encoded: In a Pogačar free-world, where the level below him in the pyramid features many riders of a similar pedigree, assigning one rider that favourite status is not easy, but one name is top of the list for many analysts: Isaac del Toro.Teammate of the Slovenian and very much built in his image, including finishing third behind him at the Tour de France this year, it's not hard to see why Del Toro is an obvious choice to fill Pogačar's shoes in races like the World Championships and Il Lombardia, though the young Mexican himself isn't quite so sure.Despite his prodigious talents and swaggering confidence on the road, Del Toro is a different character when he speaks off the bike, and has never been one to over-egg his own chances, even now."No, I will say no," he said this week when asked if he could be considered one of the main favourites for the rainbow jersey. "Everybody is super strong. Everybody has their plans, and everybody has history in these kinds of races. As a nation we're still growing, and for sure I have the ambition to try to take the main spot, but yeah, it's hard."Del Toro is right that, riding for Mexico, he has to count on a smaller, weaker team, up against squads from France, Spain and Belgium, but at the same time, his performance at last year's World Championships seemed to dispel the idea that a smaller team could hold him back.In Kigali, he was the only rider who would follow Pogačar's eventually race-winning attack, and whilst he ultimately faded to finish seventh, he proved then that – big team or not – he is able to be amongst the best when it matters in the Worlds road race. After his success at the Tour earlier this summer – as well as victories at Tirreno-Adriatico, the Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes and the Deutschland Tour – there's no reason to believe his ability will be any different in Montreal in two weeks' time."I prepare myself to be good, and if this puts me in the place to fight for it I will do it, but it's not a specific [training]," he said of his preparation for this block in Canada. "More or less my goal is to have the same shape all year and trying to do the best every race, and hoping for the best."Form-wise, everything points towards Del Toro being in a shape that certainly can compete with the best in the next few races, as he has been doing all year."I mean my level is not getting super high week by week, but I will say that I am more or less the same guy [that I was in] February, and hopefully I just can be more healthy and be good for these races that I have in the final part of the year," he said. "Let's see, if I have a good day, maybe I can be in the front."And if he can be in the front, it seems hard to imagine that Del Toro won't be able to chase after that rainbow jersey, or at least a first World Championships medal.Despite playing down his favourite status for the world title race in a few weeks' time, Del Toro couldn't help but let that confidence slip out when it comes to the races coming this weekend."Which race would be better to win, Montréal or Quebec? Which one would mean more to you?" a journalist asked.The answer was quick, and with a smile: "Both."And if he does win both, well, he won't be able to deny his Worlds favourite status much longer.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: 'You've got that pressure in your head' - Kern Pharma hit final days of Vuelta a España in last-ditch battle to continue in 2027
item.author: Alasdair Fotheringham
item.content:encoded: At a time when local fans are celebrating the renaissance of Enric Mas and the reemergence of Movistar as a major GC player, you might be forgiven for thinking that Spanish cycling is hitting a new high. However, not so far behind the scenes, things are not so looking nearly so rosy for the professional sport.A few months back when Kern Pharma, a Catalan pharmaceutical company, announced they were going to end their backing of their ProTeam at the end of 2026, there were high hopes that a new sponsor could be found in time for 2027. Instead, whilst conversations are ongoing on numerous fronts, nothing - yet - has been signed, and as things stand Kern Pharma, a team with a long and distinguished history both as ProTeam and before that as a top feeder amateur team, Lizarte, will be folding. Not only that, the future of Kern's own feeder team, Finisher, is also currently in doubt.Whilst team manager Juanjo Oroz has given riders and staff carte blanche to look for employment elsewhere, the former Euskaltel-Euskadi pro is still not throwing in the towel. Even the first round of application deadlines for Pro Teams for 2027 next week is not a definitive one, given squads only pay a small fine if they miss the initial date and then subsequently confirm they will be continuing.As for the riders, whilst there are rumours, according to Daniel Benson's Substack, that the former Vuelta a España stage winner Urko Berrade will be heading to EF Education-EasyPost, and some staff members have reportedly found new employment, a significant number are just crossing their fingers that they will still be in a job somewhere next year and hopefully at whatever Kern becomes."We're after winning a stage every day, and we're trying really hard and showing that we can," Iñigo Elósegui, a 28-year-old allrounder and former U23 Spanish National Champion racing the Vuelta for Kern Pharma, told ."But it's true that you've got that pressure and tension in your head about trying to keep the team going for 2027 and that right now we've got nothing for next year and we've got to do as well as we can for the squad. So it's difficult to race like that."I'm riding with that pressure, myself, that it could be my last race, and I have to do the best I can. It's been like that for the last few months and it's complicated."But the team atmosphere is good and we're working well together and that helps us keep our morale."Already in one 121 kilometre break through the ultra-hilly stage to Loja - which was how he won the Spanish 23-Nationals all those years ago - the Vuelta is also where Kern Pharma have delivered their standout performances as a collective too. Two years ago, the squad took no less than three stage wins, the most in the Vuelta for a wildcard team since 2012, and while the squad will continue to race both in the Tour de Langkawi and various Italian and French Classics before the end of the 2027 season, they know the next three days in the Vuelta are the biggest showcase they have left to impress a sponsor. In Elósegui's case, given he's not even sure where he's racing after Sunday, that's even more the case.It's often thought that when top teams and riders in a country are succeeding, as is the case with Enric Mas and the Vuelta a España, there's bound to be some kind of trickle-down benefit for cycling as a whole. But just as the 'trickle-down' theory of economics has been disproven time and again, that's also the case, regrettably in cycling, and Mas and Movistar's boom time does not mean their squad's former feeder team is also feeling the good news vibe."It's true there are a lot more public out on the roads and a lot more interest generally thanks to what's happening [with Mas leading the Vuelta], but the thing is, backing a cycling team costs a lot of money," Elósegui points out. "It can't just happen overnight just because it's a great time for Movistar, it's a long-term thing."Juanjo, our manager is working very hard on that front but it's very difficult to find a sponsor just like that."As for the 28-year-old himself, "I'm in good shape. I have a job which isn't so high profile because I'm there to help the teammates behind the scenes as a domestique, but fortunately I'm feeling really good. So I'm happy, and proud but even with good legs, in this kind of situation, it's complicated.""In the last week, there's not really been many opportunities for breakways, either. It's all high mountains or sprints. I've been working for [Marc] Brustenga, our sprinter as a leadout man, and then I'll try and help get our climbers in the moves in the mountains."Elósegui has always been very interested in Japanese culture and sport, and he doesn't rule out following the wheeltracks of pros like Rein Taaramae, the former Vuelta a España leader and double stage winner who headed to that country in 2025 to continue his career, in the Estonian's case racing with the Kinan Continental squad."I've always liked the country and the culture, and during the pandemic I decided to study Japanese and I travelled there, learning more and more about it. Apart from Keirin, I also follow the racing there in Japan. They've got a lot of good young riders- they're mostly very explosive because they mostly do circuit racing, so it's tricky for them adapting to the longer races in Europe."But I've thought of maybe trying my luck there, if nothing comes through here," Elósegui says."It's true that during the Vuelta, the days are so long we don't really have time for that, once we're through here, I'll see what I can do. But everybody I've talked to about it who's raced there has said they're very happy with it."That might, then, be a last-minute career solution for Elósegui, grandson of one of the top riders in Spain in the 1960s, José Antonio Momene, fourth overall in one Tour de France and winner of stages in the Giro d'Italia and Vuelta a España as well as the Dauphiné Libére - now the Tour Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes. But regardless of past glory, the clock is ticking on Kern's future, but Elósegui says there is no fixed date in the team for calling time on a new sponsor. "Talking to Juanjo, he says there's no specific date, but if the season ends and we still have nobody, I think it'll be complicated. And in my own case, if I haven't found anything by then, I'll have to call it quits on this and look for work in something else. I have to think in my own future, too."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.author: Guardian sport
item.content:encoded: Nicolas Jackson is ready to impress, Spurs are scrambled and the 199th Manchester derby takes place at Old TraffordWith 10 top-flight goal contributions between them across three games already this season, the Chelsea trio of Morgan Rogers, João Pedro and Cole Palmer are the early pace-setters for the Premier League’s most prolific, fluid and high-octane attacking unit. But on the occasion of his 100th Premier League appearance, a scruffier and more ungainly unit will be hoping to steal their thunder, as high-flying Hull try to register a top-flight win against Chelsea for the very first time. Yet to score this season but with a couple of near misses to his name, what Oli McBurnie has thus far lacked in goal contributions he has more than made up for with selfless graft and off-the-ball grunt work, making a total mockery of Steve Clarke’s decision not to include him in Scotland’s World Cup squad. The Hull striker ought to prove a real handful for a decidedly porous home defence, and a goal would be a fitting way to mark a century of Premier League appearances. Chelsea have not won any of their past four league matches against promoted opposition and, given Hull’s blistering start to the season, victory on Saturday seems anything but a foregone conclusion. item.title: Evans: Extra tyres critical to make it through WRC Rally Chile
All over bar the shouting? After limiting time trial losses, Enric Mas' pathway to Vuelta a España victory is now clear - GC analysis
item.author: Alasdair Fotheringham
item.content:encoded: 23-0. After beating Enric Mas by 33 seconds in the Jerez de la Frontera time trial in the Vuelta a España, Primož Roglič remains undefeated against the Spaniard against the clock, and has now surpassed the Movistar man in a TT on no fewer than 23 consecutive occasions. Unfortunately for Roglič, though, as impressive as this total sounds (and is), he knows perfectly well that this latest boost to his track record against Mas is essentially irrelevant, a soon-to-be-forgotten footnote in the bigger Vuelta history.That's because win or lose in Jerez, the Vuelta's stage 18 individual time trial was never about a 16th stage victory for Roglič, or even his position in the stage ranking: rather it was all about gaining as much time as possible on Mas.Roglič sought to either rattle the Spaniard's morale so severely he might fall apart in the two stages to come, or at best, move into the red jersey and force the Movistar man to fight to get back on terms.None of this happened. Instead of a predicted 90 seconds, Roglič could only manage a 33-second advantage on Mas. With only three stages left, the Vuelta's GC battle is all but over in favour of Mas.If history was anything to go by, the stage 18 time trial had everything Roglič needed for one of his famous last-minute rises to victory to begin. After all, in the 2023 Giro d'Italia, Rogličs's triumph over Geraint Thomas came thanks to a stunning third-week uphill TT victory against the Briton, overcoming even a mechanical issue mid-climb to clinch his only Grand Tour victory to date outside the Vuelta a España. And in Spain, he began his pathway to his first Vuelta triumph in 2019 with a knockout victory in the race's sole time trial in Pau against another Movistar race leader, Nairo Quintana.But credit where credit is due, Roglič's time trial was anything but poor on Thursday. Mas delivered the time trial of his life to keep well within touch of the Slovenian and simultaneously slam the door shut on all those stories about his potential to crumble under pressure. It seemingly didn't matter that Mas has virtually no experience of leading a stage race - he's only done it twice since turning pro - let alone one of the calibre of the Vuelta. But rather than things falling apart, like they did when he punctured while leading the 2021 Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana in the final kilometre of the final TT - coincidentally also won by Stefan Küng - in Jerez de la Frontera, there were no such mishaps or faltering at the last fence. In addition to keeping Roglič on a short leash, Mas also put nearly a minute into Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM), possibly the more dangerous climber of the two. Put it all together, and the road to overall victory in the Vuelta a España could hardly be clearer.In every summit finish stage since Tadej Pogačar was forced to abandon, and even one day in the mountains before that on the Puerto de El Bartolo stage, Mas has proved superior to all his remaining rivals. It therefore seems highly unlikely that even if he only has a 1:37 advantage on Roglič, the tables can turn so dramatically in the last two crunch stages before the finish in Granada on Sunday."You can never have enough time on rivals as dangerous as Roglič, Gall, or Carapaz," Mas said after his time trial. In a Grand Tour like the Vuelta, third-week ambushes and last-minute changes of fortune are always possible, as race leader Tom Dumoulin found out in 2015 thanks to Fabio Aru or as Joaquim Rodríguez discovered in 2012 at the hands of Alberto Contador.However, Aru's success in 2015 in the sierras of Madrid and Contador's triumph in 2012 in Fuente De were as dependent on strong teamwork, at least to get the ball rolling, as they were on individual audacity once the groundwork had been laid. If Mas' time-trialling ability and newfound aggression in the high mountains have been a remarkable discovery of the 2026 Vuelta, Movistar's domination and coordinated teamwork defending his top spot overall is another. At the very least, it harkens back to the years when Nairo Quintana and Alejandro Valverde were fighting for the Vuelta.For Spain, their first Grand Tour win since Alberto Contador won the Giro d'Italia and for their home WorldTour team, too, is now very much on the table. It goes without saying this isn't the same scenario as when Tadej Pogačar, the arch-favourite, was sweeping all before him before his untimely exit on stage 8 of the race. But for the first time in this year's Vuelta since then, we're in a Pogačar-like situation of one overwhelmingly likely outcome in the GC battle, and virtually no reasons to argue the opposite.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: 'He's going to be unstoppable in a few years' – Young Scot Callum Thornley tipped for stardom after narrowly missing on Vuelta a España time trial win
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: For over an hour during stage 18 of the Vuelta a España, it looked like Scottish rider Callum Thornley (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) was about to shock the established specialists and take victory on his Grand Tour debut, but he was narrowly denied by a flying Stefan Küng (Tudor) by just two seconds.While it wasn't to be for the 23-year-old in Jerez, just about everyone who commented on him after the stage was only expecting him to kick on and become one of the top triallists in the world."We're super happy for Callum. We tried to ease off him the last two days to have him as fresh as possible today, and in his first Grand Tour, I think it's amazing," said Red Bull DS Patxi Vila at the team bus."We were dreaming of the win, but Stefan Küng is a specialist. Callum is young; I'm pretty sure he will get some nice wins in time trials in the future."Fellow Scot and someone who raced alongside him in the junior ranks is the current best young rider at the Vuelta, Oscar Onley, who said, "It was really good to see. I've known he's had that in the legs for a long time."We were teammates in juniors, and he's always been strong. Now that he's figured out how to race as well, he's going to be unstoppable in a few years. He's going to be at the top of these TTs and especially the Classics as well, I think."As one of the earliest starters, Thornley had his first major obstacle to face before he even crossed the line, and that was British compatriot Ethan Hayter (Soudal-QuickStep), who had started as one of the main favourites.When GT first-timer Thornley arrived in Jerez, found some shade and rapidly cooled off at the team bus, he was delighted to say the last, even hours before he would know what his result would actually amount to."I'm really happy with that time, especially to beat Ethan by that margin," said Thronely, who grinned ear to ear."I think I seem to have managed the fatigue quite well in this race. At the start, this TT wasn't a goal because, really, just making it to stage 18 was the most important thing, being my first Grand Tour and stuff, but to beat Ethan by that, and then hopefully a good result in the end, I'll be happy with that."While it didn't bring the major GC win they were hoping for, as Enric Mas (Movistar) defended superbly from their leader Primož Roglič, there were clear signs of the major investment into time trialling from the German team, with three of their riders finishing inside the top six.Thornley was second, Roglič fourth, and Finn Fisher-Black was sixth, who also pointed to how such a performance from the flying Scotsman was certainly on the cards given his love of the discipline."I'm stoked to see Callum on the top still; it's really cool. I think he rides his TT bike every day back home, so it's nice to see it paying off for him," said Fisher-Black, speaking ahead of the arrival of Küng when Thornley still occupied the hot seat, enjoying a bocadillo during his time on there."I was hoping to get to the finish and still see he was up there, so that's good for the team. The team's invested a lot in the TTs this year, so it's nice to see it coming out on the road, and I'm also pretty yeah pretty stoked with my ride."Aside from the strong legs he showed out on the 32km course, Thornley gave big credit to Red Bull's cooling strategy, which he likened to the bizarre sight of Netcompany Ineos' riders cooling their arms down with tubs of water before the opening team time trial at the Tour de France."This is the first TT I started where I was shivering. We had a lot of stuff going on, ice cooling, you know, the thing that went quite viral that Ineos were doing, which I think originally Dan Bigham [team's Head of Performance] was doing with Filippo Ganna for the hour record," he said."That's actually been the priority to be honest, more than anything, and I noticed the difference because the first 15-20 minutes I was really under control, not over the limit. Then I certainly felt myself getting hot in the second half, but the coolant certainly made a difference."For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews. item.title: The Lego Road Bike set is so detailed, I'm expecting it to come with a mini Enric Mas! It's now less than £100 for the first time ever in this Amazon Lego deal
item.author: paul.brett@futurenet.com (Paul Brett)
item.content:encoded: Lego dropped its first-ever road bike set back in May. If you've been watching La Vuelta a España, this ultra-detailed replica mirrors the drool-worthy bikes currently racing across Spain. The 1,015-piece set comes packed with technical, real-life details that we cyclists love to obsess over.Although it's a fairly minimal discount, it means this brand-new Lego set is discounted to just £99.99, from the launch price of £109.99. Having covered loads of Lego deals on our sister sites, it's very rare to see any Lego sets discounted.So if you fancy grabbing this road bike set, either for yourself or as an early Christmas gift for the cyclist in your life, then now's the time. Unfortunately, this Lego deal is UK-only, and the Icons Road Bike set remains at the full price of $129.99 on Amazon US.The Lego Icons Road Bike (11380) is the first road bike in the Lego Icons collection. There are 1,015 pieces in this meticulously detailed set, and it includes a functioning drivetrain with a free-spinning rear wheel. Deep-section wheels, steering, plus a removable bidon and rear light complete the build.View DealThe Lego Icons Road Bike (11380) is impressive in stature, measuring over 14 in. (36 cm) high, 23.5 in. (60 cm) long and 7.5 in. (19 cm) wide. The final build comes with a stand, which is reminiscent of some of the best smart trainers, making it a brilliant display piece in the pain cave.It's also a fully functioning road bike Lego build with front-wheel steering and a fully working drivetrain. The drivetrain features a functional chain made of individual Lego 'links' that rotate when you turn the cranks, and even more impressively, it features a fully working freewheel, allowing the rear wheel to spin independently for that satisfying real-world coasting effect.I particularly love the addition of a bidon and the rear light, which immediately reminded me of my favourite rear light of all time, the Magicshine SEEMEE300; sadly, as good as the Lego designers are, there's no brake light function or exceptional 300 lumens of brightness built in here.Lego hasn’t said which road bike the set is based on, but our cycling tech experts reckon it leans heavily on some early Factor bikes with the familiar 'chunky' bayonet head tube design. Now where is that my credit card...

item.title: 'Genuine reason for hope' for Ezra Caudell's recovery as team gives update on Philadelphia Cycling Classic crash injuries
item.author: laura@cyclingnews.com (Laura Weislo)
item.content:encoded: According to the team's statement, Caudell has been taken out of an induced coma and, now that he is no longer heavily sedated, is able to "interact, communicate, and recognise those around him", giving his family, friends and team massive relief from eleven days of worrying."Eleven days after his crash at the Philadelphia Cycling Classic, Ezra Caudell remains in the ICU at Thomas Jefferson University Hospital in critical condition, but he continues to show encouraging signs of progress," the team wrote."Ezra remains on ECMO (extracorporeal membrane oxygenation), which is providing support while his lungs continue to heal. Yesterday marked an important milestone: he was successfully weaned from deep sedation and taken off the ventilator, allowing his family and medical team a much clearer assessment of his neurologic status."Caudell was attempting to bridge across to the breakaway along with Lotto-Intermarché's Milan Menten along Kelly Drive and were closing in when Caudell looked behind to see the gap behind and hit an obstacle in the road and crashed, according to reports. According to Menten, Caudell hit a lamppost and was knocked unconscious."Ezra sustained significant injuries in the crash, including a concussion and severe chest trauma. While his medical team remains focused on supporting his recovery from these injuries, his progress over the past several days has been encouraging," Modern Adventure said in the update today. Now that he is no longer heavily sedated, they said, "very much consistent with Ezra’s personality - it wasn’t long after waking that he was making jokes and sending short videos to his teammates. "His ability to interact, communicate, and recognise those around him has been an especially welcome and encouraging development."Caudell's friends established a GoFundMe to help support his family, who moved to Germany to support his cycling ambitions and are facing housing and travel expenses in addition to medical expenses for his care. The fund has raised $83,251 of the $100,000 goal as of September 10."Ezra’s family remains at his bedside, vigilant and hopeful. He is very much on the minds of his teammates and staff at Modern Adventure Pro Cycling, as well as friends and supporters throughout the cycling community."We are deeply grateful for the extraordinary outpouring of support for Ezra and his family, and for the continued respect for their privacy during this difficult time."Important milestones still lie ahead. But after an extraordinarily difficult 11 days, there is genuine reason for hope as he begins his road to recovery," the team concluded.For unbeatable coverage across road, gravel and tech, subscribe to Cyclingnews.
